spec_match.rationale: Openly a simulation, and a sound one: throughput is modelled as packets-per-event x write size / connection interval, which is the real BLE constraint the property matters for, and both lanes share the same time compression so the 20-byte-vs-negotiated gap stays honest.

interactive.rationale: Four sliders (log-scale image size, write size, connection interval, packets per event) update labels and a live estimate, and Run animates both lanes with per-lane packet/byte/time readouts and a stop control.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises pushing an image through a simulated link at a chosen MTU and interval, running 20 bytes and the negotiated size side by side for wall-clock difference — precisely what the page does.

edge_cases.rationale: Re-running cancels the previous animation, Stop restores button state, both lanes finish independently when their simulated durations differ, and the estimate line updates on every slider change before any run.

references.rationale: See-also cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/5177569273053184 alongside the sibling concepts.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite backs the API claims the simulation narrates and its 1 pass / 7 fail run here is honest for a build with no navigator.bluetooth; partial carries the vacuous user-gesture-assertion flag recorded on the mtu-probe critique.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): load behaviour observed (labels initialised, both lanes idle at 0, clean console '[ble-mtu:simulator] ready') and both screenshots render the full control set; the animation itself is click-driven and judged from wiring.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry?.assert fires transfer-simulated with byte counts and both simulated durations on completion; console is clean at load.

design_system.rationale: Everything uses design-system variables, progress fills are translucent accent-blue with black mono percentage text, and disabled button states are styled; no contrast failures.

accessibility.rationale: Sliders are labelled with live values and the summary is an aria-live=polite output, but the two progress tracks are role=img labelled by paragraphs that are empty until a run starts (an empty accessible name at idle), and the 'visually-hidden-note' class on the baseline paragraph is defined nowhere, so the two lanes' progress text is inconsistently visible.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at true 360px and 1280px: controls stack to one column, lanes and readouts fit, and there is no horizontal overflow or clipped control on either class.

openQuestions.title: Define the missing visually-hidden-note class and give idle tracks a name
openQuestions.detail: The baseline lane's progress paragraph carries class 'visually-hidden-note', which exists neither in the page nor public/styles.css, so it renders visibly while the negotiated lane's unclassed twin also renders — inconsistent, and both are empty at idle, leaving the role=img tracks with empty accessible names. Add the intended visually-hidden rule (or drop the class on both), and initialise the paragraphs with 'idle — no transfer running' so screen readers get a name before the first run.

openQuestions.title: Connection-interval slider uses hidden divide-by-ten values
openQuestions.detail: The interval slider's raw range is 75-400 with step 25, displayed as 7.5-40 ms via intervalMs()/10. It works, but keyboard users see value jumps of '25' announced by assistive tech while the label changes by 2.5 ms. Using real ms values with step 2.5 (or aria-valuetext) would align the control's announced values with what it means.

summary: A well-judged simulation that converts packet arithmetic into wall-clock intuition, with an honestly-shared time compression between lanes and a correct BLE throughput model (packets per event x write size / interval). Verified with headless Chromium 141 at http://localhost:3000/v157/web-bluetooth-bluetoothremotegattserver-maxwritewithoutresponsesize/transfer-simulator/ (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp; desktop + true-360 mobile screenshots of the idle state with all controls rendered, clean console; feature /conformance/ route 1 pass / 7 fail, honest for this build with no navigator.bluetooth — the simulation rightly needs none). The run animation is click-driven and judged from wiring, which handles cancel/re-run correctly. Remaining polish is accessibility bookkeeping: an undefined visually-hidden class and empty accessible names on the idle progress tracks.
